title: Spectral extremal problems on $[a,b]$-factors in binding graphs, and beyond
summary: The binding number $b(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum value of $|N_{G}(X)|/|X|$ taken over all nonempty sets $X\subseteq V(G)$ such that $N_{G}(X)\neq V(G)$. A graph $G$ is 1-binding if $b(G)\geq 1$. Fan and Lin [Electron. J. Combin. 31 (2024) P1.30] characterized the unique spectral extremal graphs among 1-binding graphs with $δ(G)\geq k$ that contain no $k$-factor for $k=1$, $2$. Subsequently, Tang and Zhang solved the problem for $k\geq 3$. Note that $δ(G)\geq a$ is a necessary condition for the existence of an $[a,b]$-factor in a graph $G$. For $1\leq a 1$. For $2\leq a 1$.
